pr.body:
## The false red

The nightly of 2026-09-15 (run `34948237666`, artefact `parcours-en-echec`) had two Google journeys red, both green on 09-13:

- `help-guides.spec.ts:23` — "wizard shows 4 Google API links and format hint"
- `oauth-flow.spec.ts:36` — "connect via wizard → callback → connected status and toast"

Same `beforeAll` failure in both:

```
Ce parcours part d'une base sans identifiant « google-oauth », et cette pile en a 1
(My Google (reuse test)). Les supprimer effacerait un compte que quelqu'un a connecté
à la main. Relancer avec NODALAI_E2E_WIPE_CREDENTIALS=1 … ou viser une pile isolée.
```

## The cause

`credentials-reuse.spec.ts` creates a `google-oauth` credential named "My Google (reuse test)" and never removes it. The cleanup guard added on 2026-09-14 then refuses to wipe it, because nothing in the database tells a journey-created credential apart from an account a human connected by hand — the guard only counted rows. Whichever Google journey ran after the reuse one failed. The product was never broken: the journeys were dependent on their order.

## The fix

Both halves are needed, and neither touches product code.

**The journey cleans up after itself.** Every credential an e2e journey creates is named through `e2eCredentialName()`, which appends the literal marker `[nodalai-e2e]`, and each journey drops its own rows in `afterAll` via `dropE2ECredentials()` — including when it failed mid-way. That cleanup never throws: a failing cleanup must not turn a green journey red. Applied to the four credential-creating journeys (Google reuse, Google OAuth, Airtable, Notion).

**The guard distinguishes, instead of counting.** `planCredentialCleanup()` partitions rows by that marker: marked rows are deleted without asking, unmarked rows are never deleted without `NODALAI_E2E_WIPE_CREDENTIALS=1` and are listed by name in the failure message. A developer's real Google account keeps exactly the protection it had.

The marker is matched literally — never a heuristic on wording such as "(reuse test)", which would have deleted a credential a human named that way.

The display name typed in the wizard already wins over the account-derived name in the OAuth callback (`payload.name ?? …`), so the marker survives the round trip. The name field is always rendered by `CredentialWizard`, so the journeys now assert it is visible instead of filling it "if visible" — a silently skipped fill would produce an unmarked credential.

## The proof

New unit test `apps/web/tests/e2e-credential-cleanup.test.ts` (vitest, no stack needed). The decision logic lives in `apps/web/tests/e2e/credential-cleanup.ts`, kept out of `helpers.ts` because that module imports `@playwright/test` at load time.

Verified by mutation, not by reading:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| marker check replaced by a wording heuristic (`name.includes('test') \|\| name.includes('e2e')`) | 1 test red — a human's "Work Google (reuse test)" gets deleted |
| marker check removed, everything blocked | 2 tests red |

Gates: `pnpm test` on web green (102 files, 1419 tests), `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `capacites:check` all green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01SQY7YUPXj5sftJLmm4XtGN


## Review pass (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16)

Approved with three minor findings, fixed in `35495148`. Each fix is verified BY MUTATION: apply the mutation, the named test goes red, remove the mutation.

### 1. The marker named a journey, not a run

`[nodalai-e2e]` said "created by an e2e journey", not "created by THIS run". Two runs sharing one database — `NODALAI_E2E_DB_URL` pointed at the same stack from two machines, or `workers > 1` — wiped each other's credentials mid-journey.

**Fix.** The marker carries a per-process run id: `[nodalai-e2e:<runId>]`, random per process, overridable with `NODALAI_E2E_RUN_ID` when several workers must share one identity on purpose. Cleanup claims only this run's rows. Another run's rows land in a third bucket, `foreign`: kept, and named in a warning. Sweeping what an interrupted run left behind is still possible, but asked for explicitly with `NODALAI_E2E_SWEEP_STALE=1` — never implied.

**Mutation.** `owner === runId` → `owner !== null` in `planCredentialCleanup`. 4 tests red, among them "leaves another run's credential alone instead of deleting it" and "erases only this run's rows, never a human's nor another run's".

### 2. The wiring that applies the plan had no coverage

Only the pure decider was locked. The three mutations the reviewer named all left the suite green.

**Fix.** The wiring moved out of `helpers.ts` — which imports `@playwright/test` at load time and can therefore never be unit-tested — into `credential-cleanup.ts`, where it takes the `db` it acts on. `helpers.ts` keeps only the cabling: who acts, on which database. The new tests run against a real Postgres (pglite, `spinUpTestDb`) and assert rows read back from the table, never call counts.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `=== '1'` → `!== '1'` on `NODALAI_E2E_WIPE_CREDENTIALS` | 1 red — "reads the wipe hatch only on an exact 1" |
| end-of-journey cleanup loses its marker filter | 1 red — "erases only this run's rows, never a human's nor another run's" |
| `DELETE` by owner+type instead of the planned ids (`inArray` dropped) | 2 red — the two tests above |

### 3. The marker was matched anywhere in the name

`name.includes(E2E_CREDENTIAL_MARKER)`: a human who typed the literal marker in "Display name" had their credential deleted.

**Fix.** The marker is read in ONE position: opening once, closing the name. Anything else — the marker at the start, in the middle, doubled, opened and never closed — reads as a hand-made name and is `blocked`.

**Mutations.** Dropping the closing-position guard → "reads the run that created the credential, and only in the last position" red. `indexOf` → `lastIndexOf` → "blocks a hand-typed name that carries the marker out of position" red.

A redundant guard found while proving this is gone rather than left untested: `lastIndexOf !== indexOf` could never fire, because a second marker inside the slice already fails the run-id shape check.

### Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx vitest run apps/web/tests/e2e-credential-cleanup.test.ts` | 21 passed |
| `npx vitest run` in `apps/web` | 102 files, 1466 passed, 1 skipped |
| `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web` and `-p apps/web/tsconfig.e2e.json` | clean |
| `npx prettier --check` on the three changed files | clean |
pr.title: fix(e2e): a journey deletes its own credential, and only its own

pr.body:
Closes #111, closes #100, closes #117.

Three incidents on 2026-09-15 could not be attributed, or should never have happened. Nothing on disk said what took place, in both directions: the cluster kept no log of its own, and the CLI killed pids it had written down — or found on a port — without ever asking what those numbers now were.

## #111 — the embedded cluster now keeps a log

`logging_collector` was off, `pg-data/` had no `log/`, `~/.nodalai/logs/` had no postgres file, and `embedded-postgres` holds the postmaster's stderr only for the duration of `start()`. A `57P02` in the runner was the only trace of a backend dying, twice.

The cluster now writes into `~/.nodalai/logs/postgres/`: one file per day, capped and truncated on rotation, every line stamped `%m [%p]`, at `log_min_messages = warning`. That level reads like it would drop the crash lines and does not — for this setting the ranking is `… WARNING < ERROR < LOG < FATAL < PANIC`, so LOG survives, and LOG is where the pid and the signal of a reaped backend are written. The settings go into `postgresql.auto.conf`, merged rather than overwritten, on every start rather than once at initdb.

**A defect this surfaced, which would otherwise have shipped.** `embedded-postgres@18.3.0-beta.17` decides a cluster is ready by watching its stderr for the sentence "database system is ready to accept connections". The collector owns that stream, so the promise never settles: `nodal-agents up` would have hung forever behind a perfectly healthy Postgres. This was not reasoned out — the new `postgres-logging.pg.test.ts` timed out at 180s against a cluster whose log file was being written the whole time. Readiness is now MEASURED (connect, disconnect) while the package's own promise is still watched, because it rejects when the postmaster exits during startup.

## #100 — a recorded pid is no longer an identity

`down`, `sweepRecordedChildren`, `up`'s non-postgres loop and its `taskkill /T` each acted on a number in `~/.nodalai/pids/processes.json` without asking what the pid now is.

`apps/cli/src/lib/pid-confirm.ts` is the one place that decides. A pid is signalled only when a fresh reading agrees on the executable name AND the creation tick, and never when it is a `postgres.exe` our data directory does not claim — the rule #98 built, now reached from every path instead of one. `taskkill /T` is refused over a tree holding a Postgres we cannot claim, and the rest of that tree is killed around it. `recordServiceTree` records the runner and web roots as rows rather than bare integers, because a number alone proves nothing. `down` no longer prints a force-kill command for a pid it could not confirm.

Confined to Windows, where a process table exists. Elsewhere the old reach stands and the line says the identity was not confirmed — refusing every kill on a machine that was never going to answer would break `down` on macOS to close a hole that only bites where pids are recycled aggressively.

The ownership probe is asked only when the reading actually holds a `postgres.exe`. The first shape of this fix asked it on every kill, which put a PowerShell CIM query on the critical path of every shutdown and timed out a `detach.test.ts` case on the Windows runner. The question only ever decides the fate of a Postgres, so where there is none, the empty answer is both correct and free.

## #117 — a running stack is not a pile of orphans

On 2026-09-15 at 21:05 a `pnpm dev` in the repo ran `up` against a healthy install. The pre-flight classified the live runner, web and postgres as orphans and killed all three; the turbo run then failed on `@nodal-agents/web#dev`, so nothing replaced them. Two and a half hours down.

`up` had only two categories: ours-therefore-an-orphan, and a-stranger-therefore-refuse. The product itself, alive and answering, fell into the first.

A third category is now asked FIRST, ahead of the recorded-children sweep, ahead of the port probe, ahead of every kill. When the runner answers `/api/health` with 200 AND the data directory names a live postmaster, `up` prints what is running with its pids, says to run `nodal-agents down`, and exits 1 having signalled nothing.

Both proofs are required. A healthy runner alone says nothing about which install answered, and refusing on it would stop `up` from ever recovering its own data directory. A live postmaster alone IS the orphan case this pre-flight exists for. The lockfile is read first because it is conclusive on its own, so a machine with nothing running makes no HTTP request at all — proven by a case that fails if the endpoint is touched.

`pidListeningOnPort` moves from `up.ts` to `ports.ts`, where the new pre-flight reads it too.

## The launcher keeps a diary

`~/.nodalai/logs/launcher.log`, one timestamped UTC line per lifecycle event: started, detached, degraded, recovered, which child exited, why the shutdown began, and a refused kill. On 2026-09-15 all of that went to a terminal nobody had open.

## What is proven, and how

**By test, verified by mutation:**

| Mutation | What goes red |
|---|---|
| foreign-postgres rule disabled in `pid-confirm.ts` | `pid-confirm.test.ts`, 1 case |
| `logging_collector` off, `log_min_messages` error | `pg-logging.test.ts`, 5 cases |
| `applyPostgresLoggingConfig` call removed | `postgres-logging.pg.test.ts`, all 3 cases, against a real cluster |
| the already-running refusal removed | `already-running.test.ts`, 2 cases, one of them the incident reproduced |

`postgres-logging.pg.test.ts` starts a real embedded cluster in a temp directory on a free port, kills one of its backends from outside with a `SIGKILL`, and asserts the log names that pid and carries the postmaster's "terminating any other active server processes". That is the 2026-09-15 crash reproduced end to end, and it runs green on the Linux CI job.

`already-running.test.ts` serves a real `/api/health` over a real socket next to a real `postmaster.pid` naming a live process — the exact combination `up` mistook for rubbish at 21:05.

`recorded-tree.test.ts` gains two cases against real spawned processes: a pid whose executable changed, and a recorded pid that is now a Postgres we cannot claim. Neither is killed.

**By isolated execution:** every run here used a temp data directory and a free port. Nothing touched :3000, :3001, :25444, or `~/.nodalai/pg-data`.

**Not proven, and said rather than hidden:**

- GitHub's Windows runner cannot start the embedded cluster at all — the postmaster exits immediately writing nothing, in 6.7s, while the same file passes on the Linux runner and on a real Windows machine in 6s. `embedded-postgres-available.ts` probes for it and announces the skip with the reason, the way `process-table-available.ts` already does for the process table. The settings stay proven unconditionally by `pg-logging.test.ts`; the postmaster's side stays proven by the Linux job.
- The Windows-specific cases in `recorded-tree.test.ts` skip on a machine that cannot enumerate its process table, GitHub's Windows runner included. Existing policy, unchanged.
- No real `postgres.exe` is started as a tree member in a suite, so the foreign-postgres-inside-a-tree case is proven through the pure rule in `pid-confirm.test.ts` rather than against a live cluster. Starting one would mean risking somebody's data directory, which is the whole reason the decision was extracted into a pure function.
- The three lines that call the already-running refusal from `runUp` are not themselves covered: exercising them means letting `runUp` read the real `~/.nodalai/config.json`. The decision, both probes and the message are covered against real sockets and real lockfiles.

## Gates

`pnpm test` on `apps/cli` (23 files, 219 passed, 7 skipped) and `packages/tools` (69 files, 1011 passed), `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `prettier --check` green locally. CI green: `ci`, `ci-windows`, `e2e-smoke`, `pack-smoke`, Snyk. `deps:check` reports only pre-existing `packages/db` paths that the worktree junction mis-resolves; nothing in `apps/cli`.

## Review pass (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16)

Four findings, one major and three minor. Each is closed by a test that fails
first, and each fix is verified BY MUTATION — the mutation is named in its
commit.

### Major — `killPidTree` signalled the root the reading had just disowned

The Windows branch judged the TREE and discarded the verdict on the ROOT that
`confirmTree` handed back. Its non-`/T` path ran `taskkill /F /PID <root>`
unconditionally, including the two cases where the fresh reading it had just
taken said that pid must not be touched: an empty table (`tableRead` false —
nothing was confirmed, so the kill rested on a bare number) and a table that
disowns the root (another executable, or another generation of the same one, the
caller's confirmation having been taken against an EARLIER reading). That
contradicted claim #1 of this pull request in the one function all the kill
paths go through.

The verdict is now spent, with `pid-confirm.ts`'s own codes and no second
definition of the rule:

| Root verdict | What happens |
|---|---|
| `TABLE_UNREADABLE` | nothing is signalled at all — no `/T`, no root, no member — and `KILL_REFUSED code=TABLE_UNREADABLE` says why |
| `FOREIGN_POSTGRES`, `BINARY_CHANGED`, `PID_RECYCLED` | the root is spared and the refusal printed; the members, observed as descendants in that same reading, are still swept |
| `PID_GONE` | nothing to signal, and nothing to report |
| `IDENTITY_NOT_RECORDED` | unchanged: a caller holding a live child handle has no record to offer and needs none, or every spawned child would survive its own shutdown |

`killPidTree` now takes the caller's record so those verdicts can exist at all,
and `down` hands it over: the confirmation it makes against its own snapshot is
re-made against the later reading this function takes.

Proven by `kill-tree-refusal.test.ts` at the `execa` boundary, on the real
argument arrays a Windows would have received. **Mutation:** restoring the
unconditional `taskkill /F /PID` turns the empty-table, recycled-root and
changed-binary cases red (3 of 5); the nominal `/T` case and the no-record case
stay green, which is what says the fix did not simply stop killing things.

### Minor — `postgresql.auto.conf` was rewritten in place

`writeFileSync` truncates before it writes, and this file is applied on EVERY
start: a crash in between leaves a truncated config that Postgres refuses to
parse, locking the cluster out of every future boot rather than just the
interrupted one. The content now goes to a scratch file in the same directory
and is renamed over the target. The target is not unlinked first on any
platform — `fs.renameSync` replaces an existing destination on Windows too, and
unlinking opens a window where a failing rename leaves no config at all. That
first shape was caught by the third case below, which found the previous file
gone.

Proven by `pg-logging-atomic.test.ts`. **Mutation:** the direct `writeFileSync`
turns 2 of 3 cases red. **Not proven:** a test cannot induce a power cut, so the
truncated intermediate state is not observable; the case that only reads the
finished directory stays green under the mutation.

### Minor — `up` killed a pid in silence where `down` said it could not confirm it

Off Windows, the non-postgres orphan loop forced `{ killable: true }` and sent
SIGKILL without a word, while `down`, on exactly the same evidence, printed that
no process table existed to confirm the identity with. The sentence moves into
`pid-confirm.ts` as `unconfirmedIdentityNotice` and both commands print it.

**Mutation:** deleting the call from `up.ts` turns the second case red. **Not
proven:** the branch is only reached where no process table exists, which is
never the machine running the suite, so that case reads the source and proves
the call is on that path — not that a user saw it.

### Minor — a wrong password waited 180 seconds and left a cluster running

`startAndWaitUntilReady`'s `resolvedItself` fallback cannot fire any more: with
`logging_collector` on, the collector owns the postmaster's stderr and the
package's promise never settles. A refusal no waiting can fix therefore looked
exactly like a slow start — retried for 180s, reported as a readiness timeout,
and a live postmaster left behind that no handle of ours could stop. SQLSTATE
class 28 (`invalid_authorization_specification`: 28000, 28P01) now fails loud
and immediately, naming the code, with the cluster stopped through the package's
`pg_ctl stop -m fast`. Nothing else is fatal: an unrecognised code stays a
retry, because the cost of retrying a real startup error is one deadline and the
cost of giving up on a cluster that WAS coming up is a failed boot. The deadline
path stops the cluster too.

Proven by `postgres-auth-failure.test.ts`, against a handle whose `start()`
never settles — the situation that killed the old fallback. **Mutation:**
removing the auth branch makes that case hang until the test timeout, which is
the 180s wait reproduced.

### Fifth finding, raised by `ci-windows` itself

The first shape of the major fix refused every signal whenever the process table
did not answer. GitHub's Windows runner is exactly such a machine — both
queries time out — and `detach.test.ts`'s grandchild stayed alive there, 46s of
it. That is not a runner quirk: a Windows machine whose WMI is slow or blocked
would no longer have been able to stop its own children.

The refusal exists to stop us acting on a REMEMBERED number, and a handle is not
a memory. So the same distinction the `recorded` parameter draws decides this
case too: with a record and no reading, nothing is signalled
(`KILL_REFUSED code=TABLE_UNREADABLE`); with no record, the old reach stands and
`KILL_UNCONFIRMED code=TABLE_UNREADABLE` states that the identity was not
confirmed, the way `down` already states it where no process table exists at
all. **Mutation:** refusing on both — the shape `ci-windows` rejected — turns the
new live-handle case red.

### The two docs commits are reverted, in favour of #112

`71fce0ad` is reverted by `b957f2c4`: retyping the homepage figures by hand is
the bug #112 (`fix/nightly-vs-homepage`) removes by deriving them from the
snapshot, #112 merges first, and this is a CLI pull request. `apps/docs` is now
identical to `origin/main` — `git diff origin/main -- apps/docs` is empty. The
other docs commit, `8127fd8c`, is deliberately left alone: it was a cherry-pick
of main's own `5fe6cfda`, which the merge with main brought in anyway, so
reverting it would have removed a fix main carries. The three homepage cases are
red again here, as on main and on #103 and #113 — issue #125, expected.

The paragraph below describes what those commits did while they stood.

### Two commits that are not findings

The branch was behind `main` and inherited a red `ci` job it had not caused: the
nightly `chore(qa): mesure du …` commit rewrites `apps/qa/data/snapshot.json`
and carries `[skip ci]`, so the homepage constants that cite it drift unnoticed
until the next pull request runs. `main`'s own fix for this is cherry-picked
here, and the figures are re-cited against the 15 September measurement
(`76761ae9`) that the merge with `main` brings: 565 test files, 6,999 cases, 234
end-to-end cases, 81.7% line coverage, 13 of 24 capabilities green at both
levels. No CLI file is touched by either commit.

### Open, and printed rather than hidden: `pg_ctl stop` hangs on the Linux runner

`postgres-logging.pg.test.ts` died twice on "Hook timed out in 120000ms" with
all three of its cases green. The hook has two lines and the message named
neither. The teardown now gives the stop a 60s budget of its own and says what
it could not clean, and the next run answered: `pg_ctl stop did not return
within 60s (waited 60002ms)`. The postmaster was working through the crash
recovery the third case provokes by killing one of its backends from outside.

That is a real fact about this suite on that runner, and it is NOT fixed here.
What changed is that the file now reports on its cases instead of on its
cleanup, and prints the data directory a postmaster may still hold. Worth its
own issue.

### Gates for this pass

`npx vitest run apps/cli` — 26 files, 233 passed, 7 skipped. `tsc --noEmit -p
apps/cli`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` green on every file touched.
`pnpm capacites:check` green (24 required capabilities, no unproven claim).
Note that `apps/cli/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/tests/**`, so the new suites
are type-checked by Vitest's transform rather than by `tsc`.

## Review pass 2 (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16)

Three findings acted on, one rejected on the evidence. Each fix is closed by a
test that fails first, and each mutation is named in its commit.

### Major — a bare recorded number was still an identity for the root

`confirmRecordedPid` refuses a recorded pid carrying neither a creation tick nor
an executable name (`IDENTITY_NOT_RECORDED`, the case of a `processes.json`
written before #100) and `killPidTree` signalled it anyway: the code was in
neither the veto set nor the unreadable-table branch, so the root fell through
to `taskkill /F /PID`. A refusal any caller can walk around by handing over a
THINNER record is not a refusal. No caller reaches it today — `down` and `up`
both pre-confirm — which is why it was worth closing before one did.

The verdict means two different things depending on who asked, and reading it as
one thing was the hole. With no record at all, the caller holds the process it
spawned seconds ago: nothing to compare, nothing to prove, unchanged. With a
record that proves nothing, the root is spared and `KILL_REFUSED
code=IDENTITY_NOT_RECORDED` says why, while the members the same reading vouched
for are still swept. `{ pid }` is no longer substituted for an absent record and
then read back as one.

**Mutation:** dropping the `fromRecord` clause from `vetoesRoot` turns the new
case red; the live-handle case and `detach.test.ts` stay green.

### Rejected — `stopQuietly` cannot find a process to signal

Checked in the dependency rather than argued.
`embedded-postgres@18.3.0-beta.17` assigns `this.process = spawn(postgres,
['-D', …])` synchronously inside `start()`, in the `new Promise` executor, before
the cluster accepts a single connection (`dist/index.js`). So it is always set
by the time our probe loop can fail, and the stop always has something to
signal.

The proof the finding actually asked for is now in the repository anyway, which
is the better answer: `postgres-auth-stop.pg.test.ts` starts a real cluster,
restarts it with the wrong password, and asserts the start fails with the
SQLSTATE AND that `livePostmasterPid(dataDir)` is null — the data directory
itself saying nothing of ours is alive on it. A second case starts it again with
the right password, which is what says the stop was clean rather than a kill.
**Mutation:** removing `stopQuietly(pg)` leaves pid 31088 running (`expected
31088 to be null`) and the follow-up start then times out after 120s.

### Minor — `log_truncate_on_rotation` does not do what the comment claimed

It applies to the rotation `log_rotation_age` triggers, not to
`log_rotation_size`: a size-triggered rotation on a name that has not changed
leaves more than one file behind. Both settings stay — the size cap is a
backstop against one loud day filling a disk, and losing the rest of a crash
day's log to stay under it would defeat the point of keeping a log. What changes
is that the file now says which setting does which. A wording fix, not
test-provable, and stated as such.

### Minor — two clusters truncated each other's crash history

The log file is named after a DAY, that name is emptied when the day comes
round, and every cluster wrote into `~/.nodalai/logs/postgres/`. A `pnpm dev`
stack and an isolated review worktree side by side — the ordinary case on this
machine — therefore blanked each other's history, which is the exact record #111
exists to keep.

`postgresLogDirFor(dataDir)` gives each data directory its own subdirectory,
named after that directory's last segment plus an 8-hex digest of the absolute
path, spelled the way `sameDirectory` compares paths: resolved, forward slashes,
case-folded on Windows only. One directory spelled two ways lands in one place;
two directories differing only by case land in two places where the filesystem
says they are two. **Mutation:** returning the shared `PG_LOG_DIR` turns 2 of
the 4 new cases red.

### Gates for pass 2

`npx vitest run apps/cli` — 28 files, 241 passed, 7 skipped. `tsc --noEmit -p
apps/cli`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` green on every file touched.

## Review pass 3 (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16) — closed

Three majors announced, none of them retained after checking at the source. The
minors from the same pass are fixed here, and this closes the loop.

### The three majors, and why each was rejected

**"The creation tick is compared as text between two PowerShell sources."** It
is not two sources. The recorded tick (`processes.ts`, `recordServiceTree`) and
the live reading both come out of `processSnapshotWin` — the same
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` query, `CreationDate.Ticks`, the same .NET tick
format. The fallback query emits the same ticks, verified digit for digit on
2026-08-21 and written down next to it.

**"The graceful stop only targets `pgOrphans[0]`, so backends take SIGKILL."**
`orphans` holds only processes a listener probe MEASURED on a configured port,
which is the postmaster; backends hold no listening socket and are never in that
list. The SIGKILL fallback, when the lockfile does not agree, is documented as
the risk taken knowingly.

**"`ALREADY_RUNNING` refuses wrongly."** The direction is safe — the refusal
signals nothing — and the design is argued in `already-running.ts`: both proofs
are required precisely because either alone is wrong. Retained as a MINOR about
the MESSAGE, below, and fixed.

### Minor — the refusal claimed more than it had seen

It ended on "so this is the product running, not leftovers to clean up", which
is a reading of the evidence, not the evidence. A postmaster of ours orphaned
from an earlier run, next to somebody else's server on the configured port,
produces both readings. The message now states the two facts — a 200 on the
runner port, a live postmaster for our data directory — and says what to do when
they are not this install: which pid to look at, free the port or change it in
`~/.nodalai/config.json`, then run `up` again. **Mutation:** restoring the old
ending turns 2 cases red.

### Minor — the window was documented for the root only

Between the reading that walks the tree and the member kills sits the root kill.
Each member is now re-confirmed against a FRESH reading, against the identity the
first reading recorded for it: same rule as the root, same codes. The second
reading is taken only when there are members to sweep, so it stays off the path
of a `killProcessTree(child)` on a machine whose table will not answer. When it
cannot be taken, the members are swept as before and `KILL_UNCONFIRMED
code=TABLE_UNREADABLE` says so — a reading DID happen and established these pids
as descendants of a process we proved ours, and refusing on the failure of a
second look would leave the workers this sweep exists to catch running for good.

Two windows this does not close are now written down where they live: `/T` walks
the tree inside taskkill, so a child spawned after our reading is killed without
being seen here; and the gap between the second reading and each taskkill is
smaller but not zero. A pid is not a handle. **Mutation:** sweeping `killable`
directly turns 4 of 12 cases red.

### Minor — `up` rotated around a port it had declined to free, in silence

After a hard Ctrl+C with an unreadable process table, a recorded child can still
hold :3000; every path refuses it, and `up` moves to :3001 leaving it there.
`formatPortRotation` now names the pid still holding the old port and says the
port was abandoned, not freed — and names nobody when no pid was measured, since
a Windows reservation or a ghost socket has no holder and inventing one is the
mistake #97 made thirteen times. **Mutation:** dropping the holder turns 2 cases
red, removing the probe in `up.ts` turns the source case red.

### Also closed here rather than deferred: #127

`down` awaited `pg.stop()` with no deadline, and on GitHub's Linux runner that
stop was measured not returning within 60s while a postmaster recovered from a
backend killed from outside. The WAIT is now bounded — never the stop, which is
a process and keeps going — and past the budget `down` says so and falls through
to the re-probe that already knows what to claim. **Mutation:** a bare await
hangs the case until the test timeout.

### Gates for pass 3

`npx vitest run apps/cli` — 28 files, 255 passed, 7 skipped, run twice.
`tsc --noEmit -p apps/cli`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` green over
`apps/cli/src`.

CI green on all four jobs (run 35063712080): `ci`, `ci-windows`, `e2e-smoke`,
`pack-smoke`. The `homepage.test.tsx` cases this branch expected to stay red are
green — #125 was fixed on main, which the merge brings in. `ci-windows` failed
once on `packages/tools`' `run-command.test.ts` ("times out and kills a
long-running command"), a package this branch does not touch, and passed on
re-run; `ci-windows` is green on main's last two runs as well.

pr.title: fix(cli): Postgres keeps a log, and no recorded pid is killed unproven

pr.body:
Closes #110.

## Why

`apps/web/tests/e2e/agent-flows.spec.ts` called `requireLmStudio()`, which probed an LM Studio server on `localhost:1234`. Nothing runs that server: `ci.yml` excluded the file on purpose, the e2e stack is configured with a dummy key (`global-setup.ts:108-111`), and the quality snapshot recorded it as `jouParLaCi: false`, `resultat: null`. The file had never been green anywhere we can see, and it was the only one claiming several journeys.

The portal did not say so. A journey no workflow plays was shown "never run here" in neutral grey, the same grey as a healthy journey whose report is simply missing from the current render. Both halves of this PR follow from that: remove the dead file, and make sure the next one cannot hide the same way.

## Case by case

| Scenario | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A — proactive `save_memory` | **deleted**, screen half rewritten | It asked a real model to decide on its own to save a memory. The screen half is now `memory-kept.spec.ts`; the engine half already exists in `packages/memory` (`inject.test.ts`, `search.test.ts`) and needs no model either. |
| B — mid-delegation save + delegate | **deleted** | Needs a real model, and its delegation assertion was "at least 1 child job was created" — a count, not a result (invariant #5). #107 would have passed it green. The screen half is `delegation-outcome.spec.ts` (PR #108), which seeds the rows and reads the thread. |
| C — planner delegates to calculator | **deleted** | Two chained LLM jobs and a hardcoded per-user agent id (invariant #6). It claimed no capability, so the registry loses nothing. |
| D — `query_memory` | **deleted**, rewritten | The half that can be proven without a model is the lookup itself, and `memory-kept.spec.ts` drives it through the search box: the same `search_tsv` / `ts_rank` engine `query_memory` runs on, with a second seeded fact that must be filtered OUT, so a no-op lookup fails the test. |
| E — Telegram channel | **deleted**, tag moved | It inserted a `channel='telegram'` job and waited for a model. The screen that decides who may talk to an agent from Telegram already existed, untagged: `telegram-allowlist.spec.ts` now carries `@cap:parler-par-canal-externe/ecran`. |
| F — adapter coexistence | **deleted** | A permanent `test.fixme` that had never run. |

New file: `apps/web/tests/e2e/memory-kept.spec.ts`, `@cap:se-souvenir/ecran`. A fact taught through the New Memory modal is written, survives a full page reload (so it is the row talking, not React state), comes back through the search box, and leaves the agent's context when archived. Every row it creates is deleted in `afterAll`.

`requireLmStudio` is gone, along with the nine helpers only `agent-flows` used (`waitForJob`, `waitForMemories`, `getToolCallsForJob`, `getChildJobs`, `cleanEntityMemories`, `waitForNoProcessingJobs`, `insertJob`, `triggerRunner`, `ensurePlannerAgent`) and `readWorkerSecret`, which was left without a caller. A helper that can only pass on one machine invites the next dead spec.

The nightly measurement (`qa.yml`) no longer excludes anything. The `ls tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` form is kept on purpose: the portal READS that workflow to know which journeys run, and a bare `playwright test tests/e2e` would make all thirty look never played.

`pnpm capacites:check` is green: 24 required capabilities, 0 with no proof at all. No capability lost its last proof.

## The portal

`etatDunParcours` gives the three states one definition, read by both the Journeys page and the alert, so a row's colour and the alert can no longer disagree:

- **never played** (`jouParLaCi: false`) — RED and named, whatever a local run may have said about it. The fact being measured is "guarded by a continuous integration", not "ran once somewhere".
- **played, no report here** — unknown, not red. A local render has no Playwright report, and painting thirty rows red would mean nothing.
- **played and reported** — the report decides, case by case, as before.

The Journeys page carries a banner when any journey is never played, each such row says "Nothing runs it: this file guards nothing", the overview card turns to alert on the first one rather than below fifty percent, and `explications.mjs` says in English what the red means.

## Gates

- `apps/qa`: 260 tests green, including six new ones written red first.
- Mutation: making `etatDunParcours` return a grey for a never-played journey turns four tests red, two of them on the alert.
- `pnpm capacites:check` green, `prettier --check` green, `eslint` clean on every file touched.
- The e2e journeys themselves are proven by the CI, on a fresh stack. They were not run against Quentin's stack.

## Review pass (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16)

Four findings confirmed at the source and fixed here. Each is closed by a test that fails first, and every fix is verified BY MUTATION.

### Major 1 — the memory journey proved the client filter, not the server search

`memory-kept.spec.ts` typed `clarinet`, a literal substring of the fact it had just recorded, and asserted immediately. `MemoriesClient` filters the already-loaded rows by substring INSTANTLY and only calls `searchMemoriesAction` after a 300 ms debounce, so both assertions were answered before the server was ever asked. Making the action throw left the journey green.

**Fix.** The journey now searches for `clarinets`, the plural, which appears nowhere on the page. Only Postgres' `english` stemming matches it against the stored `clarinet`, so the instant substring filter shows an empty table and the assertion can only pass once the server answers. No added wait: the existing Playwright auto-retry does the waiting.

**Mutation verified.** Playwright cannot run from this worktree, so the same proof is pinned at engine level, in two places:

- `packages/memory/src/tests/search.test.ts` pins the exact words the journey uses: the plural query finds the singular fact. Changing `to_tsquery('english', ...)` to `'simple'` turns it red (1 failed, 28 passed).
- `apps/web/tests/memories-search-is-server-side.test.tsx` renders the real component, types the inflected form and asserts the row appears only because the server returned it. Disabling the FTS branch of `filtered` turns it red (1 failed, 2 passed). A failing action leaves the empty state, which is exactly what the browser journey now sees.

### Major 2 — a comment, or a manual workflow, marked a journey played

`parcoursDunWorkflow` scanned the whole text of every workflow, comments included, with no link to an executed step or a cadence. Our workflows name the things they explain: `qa.yml` spends six lines on why `agent-flows.spec.ts` used to be excluded. A workflow triggered only by `workflow_dispatch` counted too, so a file nobody ever triggers could make a journey non-red.

**Fix.**

- `sansCommentairesYaml` strips YAML comments, full-line and trailing, quotes respected, truncating lines rather than removing them. `ci()` applies it once, so the triggers, the bench flag and the coverage flag stop reading prose as well.
- `cadenceParParcours` becomes the single definition of who plays what. It skips `by hand` workflows and keeps `every pull request` over `every night`. `collect.mjs` uses it instead of its own inline map.

**Mutation verified**, each turning `lib.test.mjs` red (240 tests): comments read again, 2 failed. `by hand` counted again, 1 failed.

### Minor 1 — the cleanup deleted across entities

`afterAll` deleted every row matching `like(fact, '%MARK%')` with no entity filter. It is now scoped to the entity of `resolveActingUser()`.

### Minor 2 — an unreadable workflow looked like dead journeys

When the sweep shape of `qa.yml` is no longer recognised, everything silently became "never played". A workflow that names the e2e directory in a shape the parser cannot decode is now reported as `illisible`, surfaced by `collect.mjs` as `parcoursIllisibles`, rendered in its own "workflow unreadable" block that is neither green nor red, and raised by `ecartsDe` as a high-severity gap naming the WORKFLOW rather than the journeys.

**Mutation verified.** Forcing `illisible` to false, 1 test red. Removing the branch in `etatDunParcours`, 2 red. Removing the gap in `ecartsDe`, 1 red.

### Finding REJECTED — "the Telegram execution proof disappears"

The engine level of `parler-par-canal-externe` is proven by `apps/runner/src/tests/telegram/handler.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch. The journey that was removed could never run in CI in the first place, so nothing that was being measured stopped being measured.

### Gates for this pass

- `apps/qa`: 271 tests green across 5 files, including the new ones written red first.
- `packages/memory/src/tests/search.test.ts`: 29 green.
- `apps/web/tests/memories-search-is-server-side.test.tsx`: 3 green.
- `node apps/qa/porte.mjs` (`capacites:check`): green, 24 required capabilities, 52 claims, 0 without any proof.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web`: clean. `eslint` and `prettier --check` clean on every file touched.
- `collect.mjs` and `build.mjs` run end to end on the real tree: 31 journeys, 31 in CI, none unreadable.

**CI on this branch is red, and not because of this pull request.** `apps/docs/src/tests/homepage.test.tsx` fails on `main` itself: the homepage hardcodes `MEASURED_COMMIT = '13329166'` while `apps/qa/data/snapshot.json` on `main` was measured on `76761ae9`. This branch touches neither `apps/docs` nor `apps/qa/data`, the same three cases failed on the previous head `51399176`, and every other package is green in both `ci` and `ci-windows`. Filed as #125 rather than patched here, because re-pinning the numbers by hand only sets up the next collision.


## Review pass 2 (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16)

One major and four minor findings, on top of `57f035ae`. Same rule: a test that fails first, and every fix verified BY MUTATION.

### Major — an exclusion in any other shape was invisible

`parcoursDunWorkflow` only knew `grep -v 'x.spec.ts'` with single quotes. Reintroducing an exclusion with double quotes, without quotes, through `grep -vE`, `grep -v -e`, or any other filter after `ls tests/e2e/*.spec.ts |` went unseen. The excluded journey stayed in `joues`, so green and out of the alert, and no flag was raised because the `ls` itself was recognised. That is the false green this pull request exists to kill, at the very place it kills it.

**Fix.** `exclusionsDuBalayage` reads the tail of the sweep line as a pipeline. It accepts `grep -v` in all three shapes and returns `illisible` for anything else, so an unreadable pipe reports "workflow unreadable" instead of inventing "everything is played".

**Mutation verified.** Putting the single-quote-only regex back turns 4 tests red, 242 green.

### Minor 1 — the page had its own definition of a bucket

The Journeys page recomputed its bucket label rather than reading `etatDunParcours`, so a bucket and the colour of the rows inside it could disagree in silence. `cadenceAffichee` and `ORDRE_DES_BACS` now hold the one definition and the page reads them.

**Mutations verified.** The page recalculating, 1 red. `cadenceAffichee` diverging from `etatDunParcours`, 1 red. A bucket dropped from the order, 1 red.

### Minor 2 — the new tests proved the parser and nothing of the wiring

`ci()` and `parcours()` lived inside the `collect.mjs` script, which runs on import and writes to `apps/qa/data`, so nothing in them could be tested. They move to `depot.mjs`, taking the root they read and the Playwright report they cross. `depot.test.mjs` runs them against a fake repository in a temporary directory.

**Mutations verified**, each red: not passing `tousLesParcours` to the parser (1 red), dropping `parcoursIllisibles` from the workflow (2 red), dropping `ciIllisible` from the journey row (2 red), dropping `sansCommentairesYaml` from `ciDuDepot` (1 red).

One correction to the finding as written. Removing `sansCommentairesYaml` from `ci()` does NOT let a commented journey count: `parcoursDunWorkflow` strips comments itself, so journeys are defended twice. What that call alone protects is `lanceBanc` and `lanceCouverture`, and therefore the "no workflow runs the bench" alert. The test pins that, and says so.

**Found while doing it.** `live-board.test.mjs` copies the collector into a sandbox, and a module missing from that list does not turn it red: the `beforeAll` dies on the import and vitest files its three cases as "skipped" inside a green run. Extracting `depot.mjs` put out three proofs without a word. The list is now compared against the collector's real imports. Mutation verified: `depot.mjs` removed, 1 red and 3 skipped.

### Minor 3 — the Telegram screen level now says what it proves

Moving the tag changed the claim without anyone writing the new one down. The test states it: this screen proves the owner can SEE who may talk to the agent from Telegram, tell owner, pending and member apart, and reach Approve, Deny and Revoke. It also states what it does not prove, a Telegram message becoming an answered job, and names the engine test that does. The sentence goes in the test rather than in `capacites.mjs`, because `ecranAttendu` is for a level with NO test and `lib.test.mjs` refuses it on a level already proven.

### Minor 4 — a killed run left memory rows forever

`afterAll` was the only cleanup, so a run killed before it left its rows in the database with no guard at the next run. `memory-cleanup.ts` applies the convention PR #118 introduced for credentials, not a second one: a marker naming THIS run, read only as an exact suffix, and `NODALAI_E2E_SWEEP_STALE=1` to claim what another run left behind. `beforeAll` sweeps this run's rows, names another run's, and never touches a fact with no marker.

**Mutations verified** against a real Postgres, 13 tests: sweeping other runs implicitly, 3 red. The entity scope dropped from the SELECT and the DELETE, 3 red. The marker read anywhere instead of as an exact suffix, 1 red.

### Gates for this pass

- `apps/qa`: 289 tests green across 6 files, none skipped.
- `apps/web`: the two new suites, 16 green. `packages/memory`: 29 green.
- `node apps/qa/porte.mjs`: green, 24 required capabilities, 53 claims, 0 without any proof.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web`: clean. `eslint` and `prettier --check` clean on every file touched.
- `collect.mjs` and `build.mjs` run end to end on the real tree: 31 journeys, 31 in CI, none unreadable.
- The docs homepage failure described above is unchanged and still not this branch's doing (#125).

## Review pass 3 (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16) — approved

Approved, with three minor findings. Two are fixed here, the third was already settled in pass 2.

### Minor 1 — the overview card answered the question differently

The "Journeys played by the CI" card recomputed `specsE2e - specsE2eJoueesParLaCi` on its own, without `etatDunParcours` and without the `ciIllisible` guard. Under an unreadable workflow the Journeys page and the alert showed no red at all, while this card announced "30 never played" in alert colours. Three places to answer one question, two answers.

**Fix.** The card reads the same definition as the page and the alert. Where it cannot know, it says so: "of unknown fate: a workflow cannot be read", and it does not turn red.

**Proof.** `rendu.test.mjs` runs the real `build.mjs` over a fabricated snapshot in a temporary directory and reads the HTML it writes. No reading of the source would prove the same thing. Its sandbox module list is compared against the renderer's real imports, the same guard the collector's sandbox now carries.

**Mutations verified.** The card doing its own subtraction again, 1 red. The `ciIllisible` count forced to zero, 1 red.

### Minor 2 — a failing assertion broke the tests that followed

`depot.test.mjs` restored its fake root inside the `try`, so a failing assertion left `racine` pointing at a deleted directory and the next tests failed for a reason that was not theirs. It restores in the `finally`.

### Minor 3 — the Telegram screen tag is narrower than the capability name

Nothing changed, deliberately. This was already accepted in pass 2 and written down where it is read: the test states that this screen proves the PERMISSION to talk, names what it does not prove, and points at `apps/runner/src/tests/telegram/handler.test.ts` for the engine level. The capability is verified at both levels; neither stands in for the other.

### Gates for this pass

- `apps/qa`: 293 tests green across 7 files, none skipped.
- `node apps/qa/porte.mjs`: green, 0 capabilities without any proof.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` clean over `apps/qa`.

pr.body:
Closes #109.

## The failure

`chore(qa): mesure du …` rewrites `apps/qa/data/snapshot.json` with `[skip ci]`. The homepage figures lived in `apps/docs/app/home-content.ts` as hand-typed constants, and `homepage.test.tsx` compared the two. So every nightly left main red for a check main never runs again, and the next pull request opened inherited a failure it had not caused. #108 synced the constants by hand; that was a patch.

## The fix

One source. `apps/docs/scripts/measured-facts.ts` derives the figures from the snapshot, `scripts/gen-reference.ts` writes `apps/docs/lib/measured-facts.json` on every build, and the page renders that file, exactly as `catalog-facts.json` is derived from the catalogs.

- Every figure is required: a snapshot missing one fails the build naming the field, never a silent `0`.
- Coverage is rounded down, so the page can never overstate it.
- The capability sentence next to the table ("twelve of the twenty-four") is derived too, rather than spelled out.

## What the tests prove now

They never compare the page to the live snapshot again, because that comparison is the bug.

- `measured-facts.test.ts`: the real snapshot yields every figure; the date is spelled in UTC; coverage never rounds up; a missing field throws with the field name; a measurement claiming more proven capabilities than it has is refused.
- `homepage.test.tsx`: the page prints every derived figure and cites the date, commit and run; it takes those values from the generated file, never from a transcription; the deploy regenerates them on each build and rebuilds after each measurement.

`docs.yml` already covers the rebuild: `workflow_run` on `Quality — full measurement`, `ref: main` so it checks out the data commit and not the triggering SHA, then `pnpm --filter @nodal-agents/docs build`, which runs the generator. A test now asserts all three.

## Verified by mutation

- Return `0` for an absent snapshot field: the fail-loud case goes red.
- Type the old constants back into `home-content.ts`: the transcription case goes red.
- Edit the snapshot without regenerating: the docs suite stays green. That is the failure mode this closes.

Green locally: docs and qa suites, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, `prettier --check`, `apps/qa/porte.mjs`, and `next build`.


## Review pass (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16)

Changes requested: one major finding and three minor ones. All four are fixed
here, each closed by a case that goes red when the fix is removed.

### Major — nothing proved the generator writes the file, and turbo could skip it

**Confirmed first.** Deleting the `writeFileSync` block for
`lib/measured-facts.json` from `scripts/gen-reference.ts` left the whole docs
suite green, 28 of 28. `measured-facts.test.ts` derives the figures itself, and
`homepage.test.tsx` reads the same committed file the page imports, so neither
could see a generator that had stopped writing. The next measurement would then
have been published under the figures of an older one, every test still green.

**Fixed.** `gen-reference.ts` takes its output root from `NODAL_DOCS_GEN_OUT`
(unset in production, where it stays `apps/docs`), and
`src/tests/gen-reference.test.ts` runs the real generator against a throwaway
directory and reads what came out. *Mutation: remove the `writeFileSync` block,
two cases red.*

**Not added, deliberately: a comparison between the committed
`measured-facts.json` and the committed `snapshot.json`.** That comparison is
issue #109. The nightly rewrites the snapshot with `[skip ci]`, so every pull
request opened afterwards would inherit a red check for a drift it had not
caused, which is the exact failure this pull request closes. Nor is it needed
anywhere else: `docs.yml` checks out `main` and runs the generator before every
deploy, so the published page is always derived from the snapshot as committed.
A stale `measured-facts.json` in the repository is a build artifact awaiting its
next regeneration, never something a visitor can see.

**Second gate, on turbo.** `pnpm build` is turbo, the snapshot lives in another
workspace, and task `inputs` are package-relative — so a measurement changed
nothing in `apps/docs` and turbo would have replayed a cached build.
`apps/qa/data/snapshot.json` is now a `globalDependency` in `turbo.json`,
confirmed at the tool level: it appears under `globalCacheInputs.files` in
`turbo run build --dry=json --filter=@nodal-agents/docs`. *Mutation: remove the
entry, the turbo case red.*

### Minor 1 — an absurd figure passed the guard

The guard only asked "is it a finite number?", so a negative count, a total of
zero and a coverage above a hundred reached the page as `-3 / 24`, `0 of the 0
capabilities` and `150.0%`. Each now fails by field name, in the same sentence
as a missing field. *Mutations, one per guard: drop the `< 0` check, the
zero-capabilities check, or the `> 100` check, and the matching case goes red.*

### Minor 2 — the workflow was read as a haystack

`expect(wf).toContain('ref: main')` passes on a `ref: main` that has moved to
another job, been commented out, or sits under a step that no longer runs, and
the gate that keeps a FAILED measurement from being published — the build job's
`if:` on `workflow_run.conclusion` — was asserted nowhere.

`src/tests/yaml-lite.ts` reads the subset `docs.yml` is written in and throws on
anything else, so it can never answer a question about a file it did not
understand; `yaml-lite.test.ts` pins its own shapes, since a parser quietly
returning an empty mapping would make every assertion above it vacuous. No
dependency added: `apps/docs` carries no YAML package and two assertions do not
justify a lockfile change. The cases now assert the structure — the
`workflow_run` trigger names the measurement workflow, the build job's single
checkout carries `ref: main`, the build job runs the docs build, the portal
render and the copy, and the conclusion gate is present.

*Mutations: delete the `if:` gate, red. Point the checkout at
`${{ github.sha }}`, red. Move `ref: main` to the **deploy** job, where it does
nothing: red — while the file still contains the string the old assertion looked
for.*

### Minor 3 — the UTC date case was blind on a UTC runner

`spellDate('2026-01-02T23:30:00.000Z')` says nothing about UTC on a machine
already in UTC, which is what CI is. The new case imposes a timezone and picks
an instant whose local day differs from its UTC day, once ahead (UTC+14) and
once behind (UTC-11), and asserts that difference before asserting the result —
so a runtime that stopped honouring a change of `TZ` would make it red rather
than vacuous. *Mutation: `getUTCDate/getUTCMonth/getUTCFullYear` → the local
accessors, with the process started under `TZ=UTC`: red. The old case stayed
green under the same mutation.*


### Merged with main

The pull request had become unmergeable, which is why no CI run existed for it:
main had merged `5fe6cfda`, which re-typed the homepage figures by hand and
restored the page-versus-snapshot comparison. Both conflicts are resolved in
favour of the derived figures, since those two things are issue #109 itself.
`lib/measured-facts.json` is then regenerated on the measurement main brought
in, by running the generator, not by hand.

### Gates

`npx vitest run apps/docs` — 42 passed, 4 files. `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/docs`
— exit 0. `npx eslint apps/docs/src/tests apps/docs/scripts` — 0 errors (one
pre-existing `no-console` warning on the generator's summary line).
`npx prettier --check` — clean. `node apps/qa/porte.mjs` — the product ↔ proofs
link holds.


## Review pass 2 (Reviewer C, 2026-09-16) — approved

Approved, with two minor findings, both fixed here.

**A zero passed every guard.** Absent, NaN, negative and above-a-hundred were
refused, but zero was not: a collector that fell silent writes zeros, and the
page would have printed "0 packages measured", "0 test cases" and "0.0% line
coverage" under a green build. `paquets`, `casDeTest`, `fichiersDeTest`,
`couvertureLignes` and `capacites` now fail by field name when they are zero.
The other two keep it on purpose: `casE2e` and `capacitesVerifiees` can honestly
be zero, and a guard refusing them would stop the build on a true measurement,
so a case asserts that zero still passes there. *Mutation: remove the zero
check, the new case goes red.*

**The transcription guard was a tautology.** "Takes its figures from the
generated file" compared `FIGURES` to the committed `measured-facts.json`, and
both sides read the same file, so typing today's values into `home-content.ts`
as constants left it green. It is replaced by a render against a SUBSTITUTED
generated file (a different date, commit, run URL and set of figures), which
asserts the page prints the substitute and that none of the real measurement
leaked through. *Mutation: replace the `measured-facts.json` import with
hand-typed constants equal to today's values, red, where the case it replaces
stayed green.*

Gates: `npx vitest run apps/docs` 43 passed, `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/docs`
exit 0, `npx eslint apps/docs/src/tests apps/docs/scripts` 0 errors,
`npx prettier --check` clean.

pr.body:
Closes #107, closes #115

On 2026-09-15, Alfred delegated "Fais une recherche sur la longueur de Planck" to Researcher. The Researcher ran three searches, emitted a reasoning block, then a single `return_result {"status":"success"}` — no text, no delivery tool (an internal job has none). The runner finalized it `completed` with `result = NULL`. `compileChildResults` handed Alfred `## Researcher\n(no output)`, Alfred read that as an answer and told the user "Recherche lancée sur la longueur de Planck, je te renvoie la synthèse dès que c'est prêt". Nothing else ever arrived. That row is still in the local database: job `538b8d53`, `completed`, `result` 0 characters.

## The contract, before and after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| A sub-agent's deliverable | undefined — `return_result` was supposed to carry it, and carries nothing | its final assistant TEXT, and only that |
| Signalling success with no text and no delivery | `completed`, empty result | one nudge, then `failed` with `empty_deliverable` |
| Which channels the emptiness guard covers | telegram / discord / slack | every channel, head jobs included |
| What the parent receives | a string, `(no output)` when there was none | `{status, summary, error, exit_reason, tools_used}` |
| A parent facing a failed delegation | free to announce that work is under way | refused: redo, re-delegate elsewhere, or tell the user the truth |

## What Hermes does, verified line by line

`D:\APPS\hermes-agent-main`, read-only:

- `tools/delegate_tool.py:661-720` — the sub-agent has no "I am done" tool. Its prompt says that when it has finished it writes a summary, and that its reply IS what the parent receives. Ported into the `## Delegated sub-task` block of `system-prompt.ts`, which until now told the agent the opposite: "deliver your result by calling `return_result` with your findings".
- `tools/delegate_tool.py:2064-2078` — `summary = final_response`; status is `completed` only when the summary is non-empty, with the comment "treat it as a failure so the parent surfaces it instead of silently accepting zero-content success". Ported as the empty-deliverable guard in `execute.ts`.
- `run_agent.py:217-222, 3006` — an empty model reply gets one synthetic retry, then the `(empty)` sentinel fails the run. Ported as the single nudge, then `failJob(… 'empty_deliverable')`.
- `tools/delegate_tool.py:2080-2130` — the parent receives a typed object. Ported as `DelegationOutcomeRecord` in `router/resume.ts`, serialized as JSON into the `assign_<slug>` tool-result.

## Three levels of proof, and what each one cannot say

- **Engine** — `apps/runner/src/tests/job/delegation-contract.test.ts`, ten cases, simulated model, every guard verified by mutation. Says the runner refuses an empty delegation. Says nothing about what a user sees.
- **Screen** — `apps/web/tests/e2e/delegation-outcome.spec.ts`, `@cap:organiser-equipe/ecran`, added to the CI `e2e-smoke` list. Seeds the rows, drives no model, and asserts the thread: a failed delegation shows the specialist's reason and no waiting phrase anywhere; a delivered one puts the specialist's own text in the thread. A screen can be green in front of an unplugged engine, which is why it claims only this level.
- **Bench** — real models, run by hand, below.

## The bench: `pnpm bench --section delegation`

New online section. It replays the incident's own task N times (default 5, `BENCH_DELEGATION_RUNS`) against the orchestrator named by `BENCH_DELEGATION_AGENT` through the runner's `/api/agent`, and measures without judging: head jobs with a non-empty result, delegated sub-jobs with a non-empty deliverable, and runs that ended `completed` with nothing in them. The agent slug is required rather than defaulted: a slug is agent metadata and invariant #1 keeps all of it in the database — the architecture bench caught the default I had first written, and an unnamed agent now fails loud with the list of orchestrators the install has.

The measurements below used `BENCH_DELEGATION_AGENT=alfred` (glm-5.3), delegating to Researcher (glm-5.2) — the two agents from the incident.

Both measurements ran against the same local stack and the same two agents, main's code first, this branch's code second.

| | Before (main, `09277243`) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| Clean runs | 3 of 5 attempted | 5 |
| Head jobs with a deliverable | 3 / 3 | 5 / 5 |
| Delegated sub-jobs with a deliverable | 3 / 3 | 4 / 4 |
| Runs `completed` with nothing | 0 | 0 |
| Sub-job deliverable, smallest | 90 characters | 6,797 characters |
| Sub-job deliverable, largest | 139 characters | 20,983 characters |
| Head job result, range | 153 – 1,688 characters | 1,202 – 2,674 characters |

Read honestly, that is one finding and one non-finding.

The non-finding: the incident's exact shape — a child `completed` with an empty result — did not reproduce in the three clean before-runs. It is intermittent model behaviour, which is exactly why the guard belongs in the runner rather than in a prompt.

The finding is the size column, and it is not cosmetic. Before, the sub-agent handed back 90 to 139 characters: an acknowledgement, because the prompt told it `return_result` carried its findings and it believed it. After, it hands back the research — 6,797 to 20,983 characters — because the prompt now tells it, and the runner now enforces, that its reply IS the deliverable. The parent's own message grew with it.

Two of the five before-runs were lost, and neither loss says anything about the code: the embedded Postgres crashed mid-run (`57P02`, "terminating connection because of crash of another server process") and the dev stack was killed twice by the session harness. The surviving runs are reported as they are.

## The mutations

Every guard was disabled in turn, and named here with the test that went red:

1. `if (false && …)` on the empty-deliverable guard → the internal sub-job test, the accepted-on-second-turn test and the `api` head-job test all fail (3 red).
2. Dropping `|| t.startsWith('assign_')` from guard 3b → the parent that sends a waiting message is accepted again (1 red).
3. `if (false && …)` on the cross-run seeding of `unresolvedToolFailures` → same test red.
4. Injecting `outcome.summary` instead of the typed record → the typed-payload test and `resume.test.ts` go red (2 red).
5. Removing "DO NOT tell the user the work is in progress" from the failure payload → 1 red.
6. Restoring the `(no output)` placeholder in `compileChildResults` → 1 red.
7. Seeding `lastAssistantTextSeen` from `[]` instead of the transcript → the resumed-job test goes red.
8. Seeding guard 3b on the output type alone, ignoring `DELEGATION_FAILED_MARKER` → the deferred-handoff test goes red.

Two defects found this way, both mine, both in this branch:

- a parent resumed after a delegation would have been failed over a deliverable it wrote in an EARLIER run — `lastAssistantTextSeen` is now seeded from the transcript;
- a DEFERRED second handoff (`buildDeferredToolResults`, "another handoff took priority") is written as `error-text` like a real failure, and was being counted as one — a real failure payload now opens with an explicit marker.

## Gates

`pnpm test` green across the workspace (runner 1,407, orchestration 251, tools 1,011, db 278, web 1,445, qa 254), plus `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `deps:check` (1,781 modules, no violation) and `capacites:check`. No migration: nothing in the schema changed.

The ten new engine cases live in `apps/runner/src/tests/job/delegation-contract.test.ts`, tagged `@cap:organiser-equipe/moteur`. They assert database rows and message bodies, never call counts.

The screen journey could not be run locally: this machine's stack already has an owner account, so sign-up is closed and the sentinel e2e account cannot exist (`global-setup.ts`). It is proven by the CI `e2e-smoke` job, which boots a fresh stack. `agent-flows.spec.ts` was left untouched: it requires an LM Studio server on :1234 that nothing runs, so it has never been green anywhere — filed as #110.

## One commit that is not about #107

`fix(docs): the homepage cites the measurement that exists…` repairs a failure this branch inherited rather than caused. The nightly `chore(qa): mesure du …` bot rewrites `apps/qa/data/snapshot.json` and carries `[skip ci]`, while the homepage constants it is compared against are not updated — so every PR opened after a nightly run starts red. A second defect surfaced with it: `rounds coverage without inflating it` contradicted itself on any value ending in .x5, since `Math.round` turns 81.75 into 81.8 and the next assertion rejects that as inflated. The figure is now truncated. The automation gap itself is #109.

## What the runner does NOT decide, and why

An earlier version of this branch had a guard that refused a parent's `success` while a delegation of its own had produced nothing. It was removed after four Codex passes, and the reason is worth keeping: judging it fairly means knowing whether the missing work got done some other way, and that means comparing two tasks. The runner cannot. Four approximations were tried, each defeated by the next pass:

1. **Never clear the failure** — false RED: the parent obeys the nudge, re-delegates successfully, and still ends in `unresolved_tool_failure`.
2. **Clear when another delegation delivers** — false GREEN: the fallback may have covered something else entirely.
3. **Clear when any tool succeeds** — three false greens at once: an unrelated READ counted; the delivery of the PROMISE itself counted, so the promise proved itself; and read back from the transcript, an error serialized as `text` or a merely DEFERRED handoff counted too. The transcript does not even give the order — `resumeDelegated` files the child's result ahead of calls that ran before it.
4. **Clear only on a delegation that really delivered** — a deferral still slipped through.

What remains are the two facts the machine actually establishes:

- a job that produced no deliverable FAILS (`empty_deliverable`);
- the specialist's failure reaches the parent in its typed record, and the delivered result carries a harness-written line naming it — so a user reading the answer also reads that a specialist returned nothing.

The prompt keeps its explicit ban on announcing work that is under way. It is now backed by a fact the user can see rather than by a verdict the runner rendered blind.

One residue found on the way is out of scope and filed as **#115**: on a tool-only channel, a job that fails after its redelivery nudges are exhausted keeps its reason in `agent_jobs.result` and sends nothing. That path predates this branch and applies to every failed job.

pr.body:
## The problem

An issue closed at 14:05 was still in "To do" on the published portal that evening. `apps/qa/collect.mjs` is the only thing that queries GitHub, and only the nightly `qa.yml` run (03:17 UTC) ever ran it. `docs.yml` rendered the committed data, so the board was always as old as the last measurement.

## The split

The snapshot mixes two kinds of fact:

- **measured**: coverage, journeys, test memory, bench, capabilities, packages. Heavy, 34 packages instrumented and 30 browser journeys played. Once a night.
- **read on GitHub**: the board of issues and pull requests, and the price of a pull request. One second, and stale in minutes.

`node apps/qa/collect.mjs --github-only` refreshes only the second kind, on top of the committed measurement. It writes neither `history.ndjson` nor `tests.ndjson`: no test ran, so no run is recorded. The page carries both timestamps in the left bar, "measured" and "board as of". A single date would age the fresh half or rejuvenate the measured one.

If GitHub stays silent, nothing is overwritten and the board keeps its own older date instead of being served as fresh.

## Deployment

`docs.yml` runs that mode before `build.mjs` and now triggers on `issues` (opened, closed, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited), `pull_request_target` on main (opened, closed, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft), and an hourly cron at :41 as a safety net for CI states, which carry no issue event. It reads with the job `GITHUB_TOKEN` and never commits: `qa.yml` stays the only writer of `apps/qa/data/`.

`pull_request_target` rather than `pull_request`, and the first push here proved why: the `github-pages` environment only allows `main`, so the deploy step failed on this very pull request with "refs/pull/106/merge is not allowed to deploy to github-pages" (run 34944913597). The target variant runs in the base branch context, which the environment accepts, and no pull request code is executed since the job checks out `main` explicitly and only renders the portal.

## Proof

`apps/qa/live-board.test.mjs`, written before the code. The collector mode is played for real in a throwaway copy with a `gh` that refuses to answer, which proves the hardest path end to end. Each guard was verified by mutation:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| remove the `--github-only` branch | 2 red |
| remove the silent-GitHub guard | 3 red |
| make both dates the same | 1 red |
| drop "board as of" from the footer | 1 red |
| replace the refresh step in `docs.yml` | 1 red |
| remove the `issues` trigger | 1 red |
| go back to a plain `pull_request` trigger | 1 red |

The workflow check first passed while the step was gone, because a comment named the command. It now reads `run:` lines only.

Also checked against the real GitHub API: 77 committed cards became 79, `genereLe`, `resume` and `capacites` came out byte for byte identical.

Not verifiable before merge: the deployment itself. `pull_request_target` and the new event triggers only take effect from the version of the file that sits on `main`.

pr.body:
Stacked on `feat/homepage` (#104), which it depends on for the design tokens.
Review or merge that one first.

## The problem

The quality portal has never been online. Not once.

`qa-pages.yml` deployed it to Cloudflare Pages, for a good reason: this
repository is public, the portal shows the internal state of the work, and
Cloudflare Zero Trust can put a door in front of it for free where GitHub Pages
cannot. That door was never fitted. Neither were `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and
`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, so the job stopped at its own secrets check on every
run. A portal nobody can open protects nothing, because it informs nobody.

## What this does

**Moves the deploy.** `docs.yml` renders the portal after the docs build and
drops it at `out/qa/index.html`, inside the single `github-pages` environment
this repository is allowed. `qa-pages.yml` is deleted. The header comment of
`docs.yml` had already planned for `/qa/`, so this is the plan it was written
for.

**Two triggers, not one.** The path filter now covers `apps/qa/**`, so pushing
portal code republishes it. The `workflow_run` on the nightly measurement
covers what the path filter cannot: that job commits its data with
`GITHUB_TOKEN` and a `[skip ci]` message, and such a push fires no workflow at
all. Without it, every night would measure into a page frozen on the day it was
first published. That was found in the Codex review of 11 September and is
inherited here rather than relearned. The build is skipped when the measurement
it follows failed, so a half-written snapshot is never presented as the state
of the day.

**Redesigns the portal** to the homepage identity. The typefaces were already
shared. Everything else diverged:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Neutrals | blue-grey | the homepage palette |
| Cards | hairline plus shadow | hairline only |
| Radii | 7 to 14 px, pills | 3 to 6 px, squares |
| Type sizes | thirty fractional values | whole pixels |
| Rail | flat list | wordmark dot and numbered index |

One deliberate difference: the accent is the connector blue, not the homepage
orange-red. On this portal orange-red already means "this is broken", and a
page where the brand colour and the failure colour are the same colour cannot
be read. So the flame carries failure, the lime carries pass, and the blue
carries everything interactive. All three are the dashboard's own signal
colours, so the family still holds.

No logic touched: no judgement, no Kanban column, no scoring. The numbered
index is a CSS counter, so the markup `nav.test.mjs` reads is byte for byte
what it was. The 235 tests in `apps/qa` stay green.

**Corrects the portal about itself.** It listed four workflows and named
"Quality — publish the portal" as the one that puts it online, with Cloudflare
"as soon as the secrets are in place". There are three now, and Deploy Docs
carries it. A portal whose rule is that nothing unmeasured is shown as green
cannot be wrong about its own plumbing. This is the only explanatory text that
changed, and it changed because it had become false.

**Links it from the homepage**, in the nav and as a block closing the
engineering section.

## How to check it

```bash
node apps/qa/build.mjs                   # renders apps/qa/dist/index.html
pnpm --filter @nodal-agents/docs build   # then copy dist into out/qa/
pnpm --filter @nodal-agents/docs test    # 18 assertions, two of them new
pnpm --filter @nodal-agents/qa test      # 235, unchanged
```

The two new assertions read `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and fail if the render
step, the copy to `out/qa/index.html`, or the `workflow_run` trigger goes away,
and if `qa-pages.yml` comes back. The portal is a standalone HTML document, not
a route of this site, so nothing in the Next build would notice the copy step
disappearing and the link would rot into a 404 in silence.

Verified end to end locally: served the export, clicked Quality in the nav,
landed on `/nodal-agents/qa/` with the portal rendered.

Closes #67.
